hook: A pen that writes things its holder never meant to put on paper is a simple premise, and this short file keeps it simple. Go in expecting a quiet, curious entry rather than a monster story. The interest lies in how the people who use it describe the experience, and in one odd experiment that goes off in a direction nobody planned.
whyItMatters: SCP-067 belongs to the long line of everyday objects that make up so much of the early wiki: a single tool, a short list of effects, a couple of test records. It is a good example of how a Safe item can still be unsettling without any real threat to containment. The tags point to its two halves, art and autonomy, and the article keeps both in view without explaining where the pen's will comes from.
thingsToNotice:
Pay attention to the gap between physical control and consent. Subjects keep feeling in their arm, and the quoted testimony describes letting go willingly, which makes the loss of control feel more like seduction than possession. The pen's output is also split in two: intimate biographies that recover forgotten details, and artwork drawn by people with no training, one of which is hidden behind a redaction.

The monkey experiment reads very differently from the human cases. Instead of a calm hand finishing its work, there is agitation, smearing ink and sounds the researchers cannot classify, and the file then simply stores the resulting page away without comment. That flat ending leaves the reader to wonder what the pen was trying to make.
